subject: physics_2
question_text: What is 'dispersion'? Which colour gets relatively more dispersed?

verification.note: From FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students (physics section), Ch.2 Ray Optics and Optical Instruments, printed p.10 — Section A, 2 marks. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. TRANSCRIPTION: the book prints a space before the question mark; it is removed here. Hand-checked physically: the refractive index of glass is largest for the shortest wavelength, so violet is deviated most and red least — the printed answer is correct.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Ray Optics and Optical Instruments · 2 marks

steps.label: Definition of dispersion
lines: When white light passes through a prism it
splits into its constituent colours, from
violet to red. This splitting of white light
into its component colours is called
steps.margin_note: First mark. The word splitting and the words white light both have to appear.
steps.why: White light is a mixture of colours, and the prism material has a different refractive index for each one. Different refractive indices mean different deviations, so the colours leave the prism along different directions and become visible separately.
common_mistakes: Describing only the band of colours seen on the screen. The definition is about the splitting of white light, not about the screen.
Confusing dispersion with scattering. Dispersion needs a change of medium; scattering does not.

recall.must_convey: That dispersion is the splitting of white light into its constituent colours when it passes through a prism.
accept: splitting of white light into its colours
white light separates into seven colours in a prism
dispersion is separation of white light into components
white light prism lo colours ga split avutundi

steps.memory_tip: One word carries the definition: splitting. White light in, a band of colours out.

steps.label: The colour dispersed most
lines: The refractive index of the prism material is
largest for violet and smallest for red.
A larger refractive index gives a larger
deviation, so violet bends most and red
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name violet and give the reason: the largest refractive index.
steps.why: Violet has the shortest wavelength of the visible colours, and the refractive index of glass rises as the wavelength falls. The order of the colours in the band is therefore fixed by the order of their wavelengths.
common_mistakes: Answering red. Red has the longest wavelength and is deviated the least.
Naming violet without the reason. The mark is safer with the refractive index sentence.

recall.must_convey: That violet is deviated and dispersed the most, because the refractive index is largest for violet.
accept: violet bends most red bends least
violet because mu is largest for violet
reject: splitting of white light into its colours

steps.memory_tip: Short wavelength, large μ, large bend: violet bends most, red bends least.

insider_note: One definition and one colour. Violet is the answer, and the refractive index sentence is what makes it an answer rather than a guess.
